page: Vultr vcg-a16-12c-128g-32vram is a Cloud GPU server configured with 12 shared vCPUs on an x86_64 Intel architecture. The processing core consists of 6 physical cores running at 2.0 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 10.67 GB of RAM per core. For accelerated workloads, the server bundles two NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPUs, delivering a combined 32 GB of VRAM. Local storage is provided via a 700 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate average capabilities across standard computational tasks, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 21080.54 and a PassMark CPU score of 20085.48. The memory subsystem achieves a read-only small block bandwidth of 1191.06 GB/sec, which drops to 102.38 GB/sec for large block uncached reads. However, the server demonstrates top-tier performance in specific AI workloads. Prompt processing speeds reach 8665.1 tokens per second for a small 135M model and 613.27 tokens per second for a medium 7B model. Text generation for the 7B model is strong at 32.35 tokens per second.

The server offers a qualitative balance of high memory density and dual-GPU acceleration, making it cost-efficient for memory-intensive graphics and AI workloads without requiring dedicated, high-cost CPU allocations. A notable tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation, which may introduce performance variability under sustained non-GPU computational loads. This hardware profile is well-suited for medium-scale LLM inference, prompt processing, memory-intensive database operations, and GPU-accelerated data processing tasks.
